text: Follow-up on the DBF NULL hardening (#6709): owner asked for an exact audit of Memo/General/Blob + in-memory + FPT handling. Findings: inline slots (C N F D T L I B Y V Q) already blanked and null-flagged (now pinned); memo null ignored the null request (fixed in #6709); Blob ('W') was not treated as an FPT-block owner at all so its payload was orphaned unscrubbed (fixed: null + pointer-replace reclaim the block; G/P already covered); table-buffering record caches now wiped on erase/clear; and a NEW leak found: every REPLACE writes a whole-table DBF/FPT pre-image under <temp>/command_undo that was never wiped or removed, so the old value stayed on disk after the session ended (also transaction backups removed with a plain delete). Fixed with secure_remove_tree (overwrite + delete, best-effort) on commit/rollback/UNDO/session end. Still missing and documented: index keys (unverified), deleted-unpacked rows, stale dirs after a killed process, copies outside the wiped buffers (PRG vars, freed strings). Heads-up for Codex: anything that adds another table pre-image or backup copy should use copperfin::security::secure_remove_tree.
